topics.title: Indexes & EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN
topics.description: Understand indexing strategy and inspect SQLite query plans.
topics.lessonMarkdown:
## Indexes and query plans

Create a small index and inspect the planner.

```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_products_category ON products(category);
EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN
SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'Electronics';
```

The goal is not to memorize planner wording. Learn to ask: “What access path is the database using, and why?”

pages.title: Understand the idea
pages.content:
Indexes are data structures that can help a database find rows more efficiently. They are not magic: indexes add storage and write overhead, and the optimizer decides whether an index is useful.

SQLite's `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` can help you inspect whether a query is scanning or using an index.

topics.title: Views & Triggers
topics.description: Learn reusable query interfaces and controlled database event automation.
topics.lessonMarkdown:
## Views and triggers

A reporting view can hide repetitive joins:

```sql
CREATE VIEW customer_totals AS
SELECT c.customer_name, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount),0) AS total_spend
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id=o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name;
```

Triggers can automate side effects such as audit logging. Use them deliberately because hidden side effects make debugging harder.

pages.title: Understand the idea
pages.content:
A view is a named query stored in the database schema. It can present a stable reporting interface without copying the underlying rows. Triggers are stored programs that run automatically when specified INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE events occur.

SQLite supports both views and triggers.

callout.title: Key takeaway
callout.text: CREATE VIEW stores a named SELECT definition.

codeCard.code: SELECT * FROM customers ORDER BY customer_id;

checkpoint.question: Which statement creates a view?
checkpoint.explanation: CREATE VIEW stores a named SELECT definition.

pages.title: Worked reasoning
pages.content: A view normally exposes query results, not a separate copy of the data.
